title: Decision: the agent's database runs in WAL, without a checkpoint on delete
description:
Mark, 2026-11-27, asked which journal mode the agent's database should use and chose WAL with no checkpoint on the delete path, knowing what it costs.

BEFORE. `mimid.sqlite` set no `journal_mode` anywhere, so it ran in SQLite's default DELETE mode with four connections of the one process writing it: the MLS and state connection, mimid-agent-store's `Database`, `Credentials`, and `PushSubscriptions` with webpush on. In DELETE mode a writer excludes every reader for the length of its transaction, each commit fsyncs the journal, the database file and the directory, and a connection that loses the race waits out the 10 s busy timeout and then fails. That is the shape bead mimid-604m records: minutes of silence on a user action under I/O pressure, worse on a loaded phone.

CHOSEN. `journal_mode = WAL` on the agent's connections. Readers stop being excluded by a writer and a commit stops fsyncing three files.

WHAT IT COSTS, and this is the part that was decided rather than discovered. WAL keeps a deleted row's old page in the `-wal` file until SQLite checkpoints, which it does on its own schedule. `secure_delete` overwrites the page in the database file; it does not reach back into a `-wal` frame already written. So for the window between a delete and the next checkpoint, a disappearing message's bytes can remain on disk in `-wal` where DELETE mode would already have overwritten them. That is a weaker guarantee than bead mimid-1vul.9 put there, and than agent-frontends.md §7.9 claims.

NOT CHOSEN: a `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` on the delete path, which would have kept §7.9's guarantee as strict as DELETE mode's at the cost of one checkpoint per deletion. Mark took the simpler change and the weaker guarantee.

WHAT MUST FOLLOW. agent-frontends.md §7.9 states the old guarantee and has to say what is true now, in the same commit as the change (AGENTS.md: answering another note's open question means editing that note). Bead mimid-1vul.9's guarantee is weakened and its bead should say so. Anything in docs/agent.md that promises bytes are gone at the moment of deletion needs the same treatment.
notes:
AMENDED 2026-11-27, same day, after measurement. This decision was taken on the understanding that WAL weakens a claim agent-frontends.md §7.9 makes in prose. It also breaks a passing security test, which nobody had been told when the decision was made.

`a_destroyed_chat_takes_its_messages_bans_and_attachments` (crates/mimid-agent-jmap/tests/chat_delete.rs:528) fails under WAL, reproduced independently in two worktrees: "the database holds \"gone text\"". The panic is on a raw read of `mimid.sqlite` itself, not of a sidecar. `secure_delete` zeroes the page into a log frame, and until a checkpoint copies that frame back the database file still holds the original page with the plaintext. So the exposure is the window between the delete and the next checkpoint, and during it the bytes are in the main file.

Mark was told this and reaffirmed WAL: take it, and rewrite the test and §7.9 to state the guarantee that WAL actually gives, which is eventual rather than immediate. He chose this over WAL plus `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` with `journal_size_limit = 0` at the destroy, which is the only option that keeps the test passing untouched while taking the fsync win, and over keeping the rollback journal.

MEASURED, which is why it is wanted: one first private message costs 48 write transactions and 192 fsyncs across the two agent databases in rollback-journal mode, four per commit; 49 with a write-ahead log, with journal creates and directory fsyncs going to zero. The echo at the client goes from 35.8 s to 11.2 s under real I/O pressure, and 1.39 s to 0.65 s idle.

THE TEST'S NEW TARGET is not a relaxation: after a destroyed chat, once the log is checkpointed and truncated, the text must not appear in any of the database's files, the `-wal` and `-shm` included. If it survives a checkpoint and truncate, the guarantee is gone rather than delayed and that is a different decision.
close_reason: Decided by Mark 2026-11-27: WAL, no checkpoint on delete, with the weaker secure_delete guarantee stated.
